cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy you're here.

cues.caption: Last time: symmetry and patterns
cues.text: Last time, we folded shapes to find lines of symmetry, and finished patterns, like Riya's rangoli.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 · Angles and Turns
cues.text: Today is chapter four of Shapes, Grids and Coordinates. It's called, Angles and Turns!

cues.caption: Turn like a coding robot!
cues.text: By the end, you'll turn exactly like a coding robot. Let's spin into it!

cues.caption: Meet Arjun at morning assembly
cues.text: Picture this. It's morning assembly at school. Meet Arjun! He's standing in line, and the PT sir is calling out commands.

cues.caption: "Right turn!"
cues.text: Right turn! Arjun swings round, to face his right side.

cues.caption: "About turn!" Now he faces the other way
cues.text: Then sir shouts, About turn! And Arjun spins round, to face the opposite way.

cues.caption: Did Arjun walk anywhere? Think!
cues.text: Here's a question. Did Arjun walk anywhere? Think about it.

cues.caption: Same spot! Only the way he faces changed
cues.text: No! His feet stayed on the same spot. He only changed the way he was facing. And that's exactly what a turn is.

cues.caption: Turn: change the way you face, stay on the spot
cues.text: A turn means changing the way you face, without moving from your spot.

cues.caption: How much you turn = an angle, in degrees (°)
cues.text: How much you turn is called an angle. We measure angles in degrees. When you see a tiny circle after a number, it means degrees.

cues.caption: All the way round = full turn = 360°
cues.text: Spin all the way round, until you face the same way again. That's a full turn. And a full turn is three hundred and sixty degrees.

cues.caption: Quarter turn: a square corner
cues.text: Now cut that full turn into four equal parts. One part is a quarter turn. It makes a square corner, just like the corner of your notebook.

cues.caption: Quarter turn = 90°
cues.text: A quarter turn is ninety degrees. That's the turn Arjun makes when sir says, right turn!

cues.caption: Square corners everywhere: 90°
cues.text: Look around you. Square corners are everywhere! The corner of a door, a window, even a carrom board. Each one is a quarter turn, ninety degrees.

cues.caption: Clock: 12 → 3 is a quarter turn (90°)
cues.text: You can see it on a clock, too. When the minute hand moves from twelve to three, it makes a quarter turn. Ninety degrees!

cues.caption: 2 quarter turns = 90° + 90° = 180°
cues.text: So, what do two quarter turns make? Ninety, plus ninety, is one hundred and eighty degrees. That's a half turn.

cues.caption: Half turn: face the opposite way · 12 → 6
cues.text: After a half turn, you face the opposite way. That was Arjun's about turn! On the clock, twelve to six is a half turn.

cues.caption: 3 quarter turns = 270° · 12 → 9
cues.text: Three quarter turns make two hundred and seventy degrees. Almost all the way round! Like the minute hand going from twelve, to three, to six, to nine.

cues.caption: 4 quarter turns = 360° = full turn!
cues.text: And four quarter turns? Ninety, ninety, ninety, ninety. That's three hundred and sixty degrees, a full turn. You're back, facing the same way you started!

cues.caption: Four directions: North, East, South, West
cues.text: To keep track of turns, we use four directions. North, east, south, and west. On a map, north is at the top, south is at the bottom, east is on the right, and west is on the left.

cues.caption: Right turn = clockwise: N → E → S → W
cues.text: A right turn goes clockwise. That's the same way a clock's hands move. Turning right, you go north, then east, then south, then west.

cues.caption: Left turn = anticlockwise: N → W → S → E
cues.text: A left turn goes the other way. We call it anticlockwise. Turning left, you go north, then west, then south, then east.

cues.caption: Never Eat Soggy Wheat → N, E, S, W
cues.text: Here's a trick to remember the clockwise order. Never Eat Soggy Wheat! North, east, south, west.

cues.caption: Game time! Arjun faces north
cues.text: Game time! Arjun is standing in the middle of the school ground, facing north.

cues.caption: Facing north. 1 quarter turn right → ?
cues.text: One quarter turn right. Which way is he facing now?

cues.caption: East! Right is clockwise
cues.text: East! Right is clockwise, so north goes to east.

cues.caption: Facing east. 1 quarter turn left → ?
cues.text: Now Arjun faces east, and makes one quarter turn left. Which way now? Think carefully.

cues.caption: North! Left is anticlockwise
cues.text: North! Left is anticlockwise, so from east, he turns back to north.

cues.caption: Facing north. 3 quarter turns right → ?
cues.text: Tricky one. He faces north, and makes three quarter turns right. Count them!

cues.caption: West! N → E → S → W is 270°
cues.text: One, east. Two, south. Three, west! He's facing west. Three quarter turns is two hundred and seventy degrees.

cues.caption: "Turn right 90° is anticlockwise." True?
cues.text: Arjun's friend Kavya says, turn right ninety means a quarter turn anticlockwise. Hmm. Is she right? What do you think?

cues.caption: False! Right turn = clockwise
cues.text: Not quite! A right turn is clockwise, the same way a clock's hands move. Anticlockwise is a left turn.

cues.caption: Coding: "turn right 90"
cues.text: Turns are super important in coding. In block coding, a robot turtle obeys commands like, turn right ninety.

cues.caption: It spins on the spot. No walking!
cues.text: And just like Arjun, the turtle spins on its spot. It does not walk. It only changes the way it faces.

cues.caption: turn right 90 × 4 = a full turn
cues.text: Turn right ninety, four times, and the turtle is back where it started, facing the same way. A full turn!

cues.caption: Next chapter: draw shapes with turns!
cues.text: In the next chapter, you'll mix turns with steps, to draw shapes. So exciting!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Face north. 2 quarter turns right. Which way?
cues.text: You face north. You make two quarter turns right. Which way are you facing now? Pause the video, and try it.

cues.caption: South! N → E → S is a half turn
cues.text: South! North to east is one turn. East to south is two. Two quarter turns make a half turn, so you face the opposite way. Brilliant!

cues.caption: 90° quarter · 180° half · 360° full
cues.text: Let's remember. Ninety degrees is a quarter turn. One hundred and eighty is a half turn. And three hundred and sixty is a full turn.

cues.caption: 4 quarter turns bring you back
cues.text: Four quarter turns bring you all the way back.

cues.caption: Right turn = clockwise: N → E → S → W
cues.text: A right turn is clockwise. North, east, south, west.

cues.caption: A turn changes where you face
cues.text: And a turn changes where you face, not where you stand.

cues.caption: Chapter 4 done!
cues.text: Chapter four, done! You can turn like a coding turtle, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
